recentItems.title: "We will not back down": Putin whined to Trump on the phone. Kremlin burns bridges for negotiations
recentItems.description:
In a call with Trump, Putin accused Ukraine of stalling the peace process and confirmed that the Kremlin's military goals remain unchanged. Moscow rejects compromises from Kyiv and Washington, though U.S. envoys may return to Russia in late October. Russia needs 300,000 new recruits by the end of the year to cover its losses, while its oil refineries remain under pressure from Ukrainian strikes. Meanwhile, the EU is preparing its largest sanctions package since the start of the war. Kaja Kallas opposes easing restrictions on Russian diesel, whilst the Baltic states support a ban on the transit of Russian grain.

recentItems.title: Russia DESTROYS Trump's "energy ceasefire". Ukraine prepares a harsh response!
recentItems.description:
The EU is discussing sanctions against Russia, while Ukraine calls for cutting off the Kremlin's access to foreign weapons-manufacturing technology. At a meeting in Luxembourg, Andrii Sybiha demands increased pressure on the aggressor. Meanwhile, a statement emerged in the UK regarding Russian interference in the 2016 Brexit referendum. According to reports, the Russian army lost 50,000 troops in September, with approximately 28,000 killed. How can sanctions impact Russia's war machine, and what do such heavy losses mean for the Kremlin? Watch our report to find out.

recentItems.title: PUTIN spent $200 BILLION on WAR — Ukraine just wiped out $100 MILLION in ONE STRIKE!
recentItems.description:
While Vladimir Putin raises Russia’s military spending to a record $200 billion, Ukraine’s Defense Forces have created a military-economic hell for the invaders, carrying out a series of devastating strikes deep behind enemy lines.

This week, Ukrainian long-range drones struck Europe’s largest oil-storage facility twice and flew more than 3,000 kilometers to deliver a repeat strike on Russia’s largest oil refinery in Omsk. At the same time, two Russian fighter jets were destroyed on the ground at an airfield 500 kilometers from the border, with one of them valued at $100 million.

An attack on a sanctioned defense machine-tool plant in Ryazan region led to a complete shutdown of Russia’s largest cloud provider, while Ukrainian drone operators disabled three Russian air-defense systems, striking one of them twice in a single mission. According to Ukraine’s General Staff, Russian losses exceeded 15,000 killed and wounded in just this week.

recentItems.title: TRUMP’S DIESEL DEAL: helping PUTIN fund THE WAR?
recentItems.description:
The United States has eased sanctions against Russia in exchange for diesel supplies, drawing sharp criticism for helping finance the Kremlin’s war machine. In response, Ukraine’s Defense Forces have intensified strikes on Russian oil refineries and fuel depots deep behind enemy lines.

Meanwhile, peace consultations between Ukraine and the United States in Miami ended without results. Against this backdrop, Volodymyr Zelenskyy called on Washington to ensure uninterrupted access to Starlink for Ukraine’s Armed Forces and to provide the means to secure control over Ukraine’s skies.

At the same time, France tested a modernized nuclear missile to deter Russia, while massive Ukrainian drone strikes on the front line increased Russian infantry losses by nearly 40%.
